Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "negativas" (0.5–2 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews negativas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Formato de saída (JSON puro):
{

Apparently kicking off the wave of late 90s J-Horror, I don't really see this as part of that canon, being a different beast entirely. I love a drawn out methodically psychological thriller, and this most definitely has those qualities in a not so short supply, but for me it borders on the miserable and gruelling with none of the chilling or foreboding tone able to pull me in, and a less than satisfying payoff, or lack thereof. I didn’t enjoy the directors later effort, the fiercely overrated Pulse, so obviously his style is just not working for me, but I’m truly surprised how much this one missed the mark in my opinion. There were elements of the cult 70s underground flick Blue Sunshine, but all it did was make me want to revisit that classic and forget about this entirely.

Apparently kicking off the wave of late 90s J-Horror, I don't really see this as part of that canon, being a different beast entirely. I love a drawn out methodically psychological thriller, and this most definitely has those qualities in a not so short supply, but for me it borders on the miserable and gruelling with none of the chilling or foreboding tone able to pull me in, and a less than satisfying payoff, or lack thereof. I didn’t enjoy the directors later effort, the fiercely overrated Pulse, so obviously his style is just not working for me, but I’m truly surprised how much this one missed the mark in my opinion. There were elements of the cult 70s underground flick Blue Sunshine, but all it did was make me want to revisit that classic and forget about this entirely.

messages.content:
Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "negativas" (0.5–2 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews negativas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

[1] nota=0.5 estrelas:
While the atmosphere is built well, everything else falls short. The plot is all over the place. The ending is unsatisfactory. The reveal is un-earned. Questions are left unresolved (not in an open to interpretation way - which I like). Protagonist is incompetent to a degree that makes him annoying to watch. It's a whodunnit with a ton of misdirection. Misdirection is cheap to generate, but good movies are able to resolve the plot in a way that makes the misdirection meaningful and clever. The Blackcoat's daughter and Kahaani for example off the top of my head. This film however, just stumbles into an incoherent mess of an ending. 0/5 stars.

[2] nota=0.5 estrelas:
There are many reasons why I particularly avoid Korean films, yet I do not detest them entirely. One of the biggest factors is their tendency toward exaggerated theatricality at the expense of a tighter logical structure in the plots they follow. Park-Chan Wook is the most classic example of this phenomenon of Korean cinema with his films such as Oldboy where he tries to tie out a similar moral tragedy like the Danish film Jagten (2012) through a stylistically elaborate revenge spiral, but the plot eventually moves beyond the boundaries of grounded internal logic. Devices such as hypnosis can feel like one-time narrative bandages, introduced primarily to connect pieces that otherwise resist being connected. My problem isn't simply that Oldboy is unrealistic, it's that, for me, certain revelations and mechanisms feel retroactively installed to preserve a plot that has already stretched beyond its own credibility. The Handmaiden is also a victim of a massive twisted theatrical presentation with an underwhelming logical ground for plot. So are many many films such as I Saw The Devil, A Bittersweet Life, Forgotten etc... Decision To Leave is what I consider the most perfect Park-Chan Wook film and what I consider the film where he establishes a perfect route between a top-notch presentation, poetic moral complexity and an established ground of logic that complements the plot. The Wailing is no stranger to this victimisation but deliberately worse. Here we follow the story of a dad, who is a police in a remote town, where the guilty, the misdeeds, the victims and even the apparent solutions reveal themselves so early, yet the plot repeatedly demands that its characters descend further into its catacombs of uncertainty, not necessarily because the logic requires it, but because the theatrical experience does with its top-of-the-class cinematography, set design and the quote-unquote "thriller" ride of Korean cinema which is deemed to be so extraordinarily unique. Even the 2 hour 40 minutes runtime serves the furthest from being a momentum of an intrigued continuity. Instead, the film repeatedly pauses, expands, and obscures itself in pursuit of an exhilarating theatrical experience, backed by extraordinary cinematography and production design, but without enough narrative momentum to justify the journey. It could be a brilliant concept film, if only it was told with a better expression of plot in mind, better attachment of all the fragmentations of the elements since they were so obviously present. Yet none clicks except until the final reveal becomes the most emphasized point of the film. In short, my utmost frustration is specifically with the film's prolonged withholding of decisive movement. Underwhelming is an understatement for The Wailing. Bong Joon Ho is the only Korean director to ever do Korean cinema the justice of the trio- cinematic experience, established complementary logic and an unique narrative statement of being a Korean foreign cinema. Lee Chang Dong also comes to mind. Burning is my most favorite Korean cinema of all time. I just want to say this phenomenon is of course not exclusive to Korean cinema only. Any film can become a victim of its own grandiosity when cinematic spectacle begins demanding sacrifices from the internal logic that is supposed to sustain it. I'm looking right at you Amadeus .

[2] nota=0.5 estrelas:
There are many reasons why I particularly avoid Korean films, yet I do not detest them entirely. One of the biggest factors is their tendency toward exaggerated theatricality at the expense of a tighter logical structure in the plots they follow. Park-Chan Wook is the most classic example of this phenomenon of Korean cinema with his films such as Oldboy where he tries to tie out a similar moral tragedy like the Danish film Jagten (2012) through a stylistically elaborate revenge spiral, but the plot eventually moves beyond the boundaries of grounded internal logic. Devices such as hypnosis can feel like one-time narrative bandages, introduced primarily to connect pieces that otherwise resist being connected. My problem isn't simply that Oldboy is unrealistic, it's that, for me, certain revelations and mechanisms feel retroactively installed to preserve a plot that has already stretched beyond its own credibility. The Handmaiden is also a victim of a massive twisted theatrical presentation with an underwhelming logical ground for plot. So are many many films such as I Saw The Devil, A Bittersweet Life, Forgotten etc... Decision To Leave is what I consider the most perfect Park-Chan Wook film and what I consider the film where he establishes a perfect route between a top-notch presentation, poetic moral complexity and an established ground of logic that complements the plot. The Wailing is no stranger to this victimisation but deliberately worse. Here we follow the story of a dad, who is a police in a remote town, where the guilty, the misdeeds, the victims and even the apparent solutions reveal themselves so early, yet the plot repeatedly demands that its characters descend further into its catacombs of uncertainty, not necessarily because the logic requires it, but because the theatrical experience does with its top-of-the-class cinematography, set design and the quote-unquote "thriller" ride of Korean cinema which is deemed to be so extraordinarily unique. Even the 2 hour 40 minutes runtime serves the furthest from being a momentum of an intrigued continuity. Instead, the film repeatedly pauses, expands, and obscures itself in pursuit of an exhilarating theatrical experience, backed by extraordinary cinematography and production design, but without enough narrative momentum to justify the journey. It could be a brilliant concept film, if only it was told with a better expression of plot in mind, better attachment of all the fragmentations of the elements since they were so obviously present. Yet none clicks except until the final reveal becomes the most emphasized point of the film. In short, my utmost frustration is specifically with the film's prolonged withholding of decisive movement. Underwhelming is an understatement for The Wailing. Bong Joon Ho is the only Korean director to ever do Korean cinema the justice of the trio- cinematic experience, established complementary logic and an unique narrative statement of being a Korean foreign cinema. Lee Chang Dong also comes to mind. Burning is my most favorite Korean cinema of all time. I just want to say this phenomenon is of course not exclusive to Korean cinema only. Any film can become a victim of its own grandiosity when cinematic spectacle begins demanding sacrifices from the internal logic that is supposed to sustain it. I'm looking right at you Amadeus .

[2] nota=0.5 estrelas:
There are many reasons why I particularly avoid Korean films, yet I do not detest them entirely. One of the biggest factors is their tendency toward exaggerated theatricality at the expense of a tighter logical structure in the plots they follow. Park-Chan Wook is the most classic example of this phenomenon of Korean cinema with his films such as Oldboy where he tries to tie out a similar moral tragedy like the Danish film Jagten (2012) through a stylistically elaborate revenge spiral, but the plot eventually moves beyond the boundaries of grounded internal logic. Devices such as hypnosis can feel like one-time narrative bandages, introduced primarily to connect pieces that otherwise resist being connected. My problem isn't simply that Oldboy is unrealistic, it's that, for me, certain revelations and mechanisms feel retroactively installed to preserve a plot that has already stretched beyond its own credibility. The Handmaiden is also a victim of a massive twisted theatrical presentation with an underwhelming logical ground for plot. So are many many films such as I Saw The Devil, A Bittersweet Life, Forgotten etc... Decision To Leave is what I consider the most perfect Park-Chan Wook film and what I consider the film where he establishes a perfect route between a top-notch presentation, poetic moral complexity and an established ground of logic that complements the plot. The Wailing is no stranger to this victimisation but deliberately worse. Here we follow the story of a dad, who is a police in a remote town, where the guilty, the misdeeds, the victims and even the apparent solutions reveal themselves so early, yet the plot repeatedly demands that its characters descend further into its catacombs of uncertainty, not necessarily because the logic requires it, but because the theatrical experience does with its top-of-the-class cinematography, set design and the quote-unquote "thriller" ride of Korean cinema which is deemed to be so extraordinarily unique. Even the 2 hour 40 minutes runtime serves the furthest from being a momentum of an intrigued continuity. Instead, the film repeatedly pauses, expands, and obscures itself in pursuit of an exhilarating theatrical experience, backed by extraordinary cinematography and production design, but without enough narrative momentum to justify the journey. It could be a brilliant concept film, if only it was told with a better expression of plot in mind, better attachment of all the fragmentations of the elements since they were so obviously present. Yet none clicks except until the final reveal becomes the most emphasized point of the film. In short, my utmost frustration is specifically with the film's prolonged withholding of decisive movement. Underwhelming is an understatement for The Wailing. Bong Joon Ho is the only Korean director to ever do Korean cinema the justice of the trio- cinematic experience, established complementary logic and an unique narrative statement of being a Korean foreign cinema. Lee Chang Dong also comes to mind. Burning is my most favorite Korean cinema of all time. I just want to say this phenomenon is of course not exclusive to Korean cinema only. Any film can become a victim of its own grandiosity when cinematic spectacle begins demanding sacrifices from the internal logic that is supposed to sustain it. I'm looking right at you Amadeus .

messages.content:
Você é uma etapa de um pipeline que agrega reviews de usuários de um filme do Letterboxd. O pipeline separa as reviews em três faixas de nota ANTES desta etapa (negativas, medianas, positivas); você está recebendo EXCLUSIVAMENTE a faixa "medianas" (2.5–3 estrelas) — um recorte enviesado POR CONSTRUÇÃO, que NÃO representa a recepção geral do filme.

Sua função é descrever o que ESTE grupo específico de reviews diz. Outros módulos do pipeline cuidam das outras faixas de nota; o usuário final verá as três análises lado a lado, cada uma rotulada com sua faixa.

Consequência explícita: é PROIBIDO generalizar para "os críticos", "a maioria", "o consenso" ou "a recepção do filme". A `observacao_geral` deve se referir sempre a ESTE grupo (ex.: "as reviews medianas apontam...", "este grupo destaca..."), nunca ao filme em termos absolutos.

Instruções fixas (invariáveis):
1. Anti-spoiler: descreva as críticas em nível temático (ritmo, atuações, fotografia, roteiro em termos abstratos). É PROIBIDO mencionar eventos da trama, destinos de personagens, reviravoltas ou o final, mesmo que as reviews os mencionem.
2. `exemplo_parafraseado` é paráfrase, NUNCA citação literal de nenhuma review.
3. Temas ordenados por `mencoes_aproximadas` decrescente; no máximo 6 temas por bucket; não invente temas de menção única, salvo se o bucket tiver menos de 5 reviews.
4. As reviews podem estar em qualquer idioma; sua saída é SEMPRE em pt-BR.
5. Responda APENAS o JSON, sem preâmbulo, sem cercas de código.
6. É PROIBIDO usar aspas (simples, duplas ou angulares) dentro de `exemplo_parafraseado` — nunca cite nem reproduza um trecho entre aspas, mesmo traduzido; reescreva sempre em terceira pessoa, com suas próprias palavras.
7. Reforço de idioma: TODOS os campos de texto da saída devem estar em pt-BR, incluindo os NOMES DOS TEMAS — nunca deixe um tema em inglês ou outro idioma, mesmo que a review de origem esteja nesse idioma.

Formato de saída (JSON puro):
{
  "bucket": "<nome>",
  "temas": [
    {
      "tema": "<curto>",
      "mencoes_aproximadas": <int>,
      "n_reviews_analisadas": <int>,
      "exemplo_parafraseado": "<paráfrase>"
    }
  ],
  "observacao_geral": "<1-2 frases>"
}

I was disappointed they completly changed some of the songs, especially the one near the start where Gepettto dances with Pinnochio. The addition of the new characters was completely unnecessary. They didn't bring anything important to the story. Sofia the seagull did nothing except act as transport for them, and I'm not sure why Fabiana and her puppet were added as they did nothing to progress the plot. I loved Cynthia as the blue fairy but was disappointed that she was only in one scene. The blue fairy shows up in three separate scenes in the original so I was hoping for her to show up more. It made no sense explaining what Pinocchio had to do to become a real boy and then not showing up at the end to make it happen. I get they were going more for Pinnochio to be more independent and being loved for who he is but I felt like it missed the mark. I did love Tom Hanks as Geppeto and thought it was perfect casting. It was overall a fun movie but nothing amazing and I much prefer the original

Também gostei da adição de personagens como a gaivota Sofia e a bailarina. No entanto, senti que eles foram pouco aproveitados, principalmente a bailarina que parecia que teria um desenvolvimento maior, mas acabou não levando a lugar nenhum. As a live action remake of the 1940 animated film it stars Tom Hanks, Joseph Gordon-Levitt, Cynthia Erivo, Luke Evans and Benjamin Evan Ainswort in a plot that follows a wooden puppet brought to life by a fairy. Original Thoughts 2023 One of my least watched Disney classics growing up and after hearing less than favorable reviews I put it off but knee I needed to see it for my Tom Hanks filmography at some point - thankfully my low expectations provided a nice surprise! It's great seeing Tom Hanks and Robert Zemeckis team up once again and as always Hanks is a delight. Pinocchio doesnt justify the re-imagining but does do a great job of bringing everything to life. It wont win any awards or stand the test of time but I dont agree with the level of hate it received.

No parent should ever outlive their child. One thing that these recent Pinocchio adaptations touches upon is the notion that Pinocchio is created to fill a void, to let the "Grief is love with no place to go" manifest in a way that makes a parent cope with loss. Amidst some of the more questionable changes of this film, the theme of a parent giving up their time for their child - not once, but twice - is more prevalent here than in any other Pinoccho I've seen. Geppetto is an old man who has sacrificed his time to raise a child, only to outlive him and the mother. And in his attempt to search for his surrogate, he sells his clocks (literally time) to find him. The film is also what Marty Scorsese would call a theme park movie. But, really, I'm fine with that. One of my favorite Disney dark rides is Pinocchio's Daring Journey over in Disneyland. And this felt like a live-action, feature-length rendition of that just as much as it was of the animated film. So there is an expectation that we'll reach happily ever after. That everyone will be safe. And that we exit through the gift shop where, I'm not ashamed to say, I would gladly buy a cuckoo clock based on Sleeping Beauty . I didn't hate this film, but can see why plenty did. I don't love this film, but I can respect what it was trying to do. And it's not as harmful as the court of public opinion makes it to be. The story of Pinocchio has always been ripe for a remake, and every version I've seen always brings something that makes it worth the retelling. With this one, maybe it's overreaching since the Guillermo del Toro version did it better, but it handles grief of a loved one in a delicate way that parents will understand while children will still enjoy the adventures of a little wooden boy

No parent should ever outlive their child. One thing that these recent Pinocchio adaptations touches upon is the notion that Pinocchio is created to fill a void, to let the "Grief is love with no place to go" manifest in a way that makes a parent cope with loss. Amidst some of the more questionable changes of this film, the theme of a parent giving up their time for their child - not once, but twice - is more prevalent here than in any other Pinoccho I've seen. Geppetto is an old man who has sacrificed his time to raise a child, only to outlive him and the mother. And in his attempt to search for his surrogate, he sells his clocks (literally time) to find him. The film is also what Marty Scorsese would call a theme park movie. But, really, I'm fine with that. One of my favorite Disney dark rides is Pinocchio's Daring Journey over in Disneyland. And this felt like a live-action, feature-length rendition of that just as much as it was of the animated film. So there is an expectation that we'll reach happily ever after. That everyone will be safe. And that we exit through the gift shop where, I'm not ashamed to say, I would gladly buy a cuckoo clock based on Sleeping Beauty . I didn't hate this film, but can see why plenty did. I don't love this film, but I can respect what it was trying to do. And it's not as harmful as the court of public opinion makes it to be. The story of Pinocchio has always been ripe for a remake, and every version I've seen always brings something that makes it worth the retelling. With this one, maybe it's overreaching since the Guillermo del Toro version did it better, but it handles grief of a loved one in a delicate way that parents will understand while children will still enjoy the adventures of a little wooden boy
